unmapped_findings: Standard-route A5 (900 °C/5 min + WQ, from the initial HR at 1 rpm + CR route) showed premature tensile failure driven by B2 stringer band de-cohesion; the improved properties quoted in the abstract (~1 GPa YS, 28% total elongation, 1.72 kJ/mol toughness) belong to the modified high-speed-HR route (Figure 6), not this standard-route A5 sample.
The IG-B2 is finer in A5 and tends to grow bigger into a needle shape through mutual coalescence in shear bands during annealing for 30 min (Figure 3d–f).
Total IG-B2 phase fraction = 3.7% (2.6% in URE-γ + 1.1% in RE-γ), consistent with the 3.7% IG-B2 mentioned in b0033.

γ-matrix phase fraction is reported as 64% in the modified-route strain-hardening discussion (b0033, b0046); it is not clearly attributable to standard-route A5 and was therefore not assigned to the A5 phase fraction fields.

TEM-EDX (Figure 4, on the longer-annealed A30) identified the B2 phase as Fe(Ni,Mn)Al with negligible carbon solubility; this B2 phase identity is alloy-level information relevant to A5's B2 stringer bands, IG-B2 and GB-B2.
